posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
homebrew installs bins in /opt/homebrew/bin
so your homebrew’s bash will be installed in /opt/homebrew/bin/bash.

Not in /usr/local/bin/bash

posts.name: Dalyodh Singh
posts.cooked: please tell me what should I do to exit from here

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
What do you mean exit? If you want to close your terminal app press the red button at the top.

This is not inside anything, on the contrary it has not even entered the shell as it can’t find it in the path specified. Open the correct path bash as mentioned, it should work

posts.name: Dalyodh Singh
posts.cooked: I am not able to go to home directory or write anything on terminal please guide me brother

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
As mentioned earlier, you cannot do anything from the shell as your terminal emulator itself is opening the wrong shell path, so the shell is not opened.

Change the path to your shell in your terminal emulator’s settings.

posts.name: User
posts.cooked:
It looks like the default shell on your system (/usr/local/bin/bash) is changed or not found after updation.

Use a normal editor to open the following file: /etc/passwd from the FIle Manager.

Find your username in the file and ensure the shell path is /bin/bash:

From:- username:x:1000:1000:User_Name:/home/Login_folder:/usr/local/bin/bash
To:- username:x:1000:1000:User_Name:/home/Login_folder:/bin/bash

posts.name: Dalyodh Singh
posts.cooked:
Thanks a lot to both Sarath an Sayan , now I got it

I followed these steps :
Go to Directory utilities
and change Search Path from Automatic to Local Directory and it resolves my issue now

Once again thanks a lot for both contribution
@sayan @21f1002877
Regards,
Dalyodh Singh
